title: Calibration runbook and QA harness for asymmetric INT8/FP8 reranker profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Runbook to create, validate, and promote asymmetric INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles for the reranker model family used in ranking pipelines. This ticket captures calibration methodology, datasets, acceptance thresholds for ranking quality (NDCG/MRR), the QA harness for deterministic regression checks, and rollout guardrails for Canary/Prod. The goal is to produce reproducible profiles that reduce cost/latency while bounding ranking quality regressions for critical customers.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible calibration procedure for asymmetric INT8 and FP8 profiles checked into artifacts/quant-profiles/ with version tags.
NDCG@10 regression <= 0.25 percentage points absolute for the primary dataset compared to fp32 baseline OR statistically indistinguishable (p>0.05) using bootstrapped samples.
MRR@10 regression <= 0.15 percentage points absolute on cross-traffic holdout set.
Automated QA harness that runs nightly against staged traffic and emits alerts when any metric breach occurs.
Canary checklist for rollout including sample size, traffic ramp plan, and monitoring dashboards configured in Console (route: reranker/quant-canary).
calibration_steps: 1) Prepare calibration corpus: sample 250k unique (query, candidate list) tuples from 30-day production logs, stratify by query frequency and length.
2) Convert training checkpoints to quantization-ready format (fold biases, fuse matmul/linear ops where applicable).
3) For INT8: run asymmetric per-channel activation and weight calibration using KL divergence and MSE sweeps across 5 scale candidate sets.
4) For FP8: run dynamic range estimation and validate exponent/scale settings with 1k warm-up mini-batches to stabilize outlier handling.
5) Produce candidate profiles: int8-asym-v1, int8-asym-v2 (aggressive clipping), fp8-dyn-v1.
6) Run end-to-end inference on calibration corpus to collect logits/scores and reconstruct ranking lists for metric computation.
7) Archive quantized model artifacts, calibration histograms, and per-layer scale tables to artifacts/quant-profiles/<profile>/.
8) Run QA harness (see evaluation steps) and produce a human-readable report in reports/quant-eval/<profile>/report-YYYYMMDD.md.
eval_datasets: primary_holdout: 50k queries sampled from production (diverse domains)
cross_traffic_holdout: 10k queries from non-search consumer routes
adversarial_set: 2k long-tail queries and heavy-token prompts
offline_relevance_set: curated editorial labels (2k queries) used for sanity NDCG checks
new_profile_metrics: stat_significance: int8-asym-v1 p=0.11 (not significant), int8-asym-v2 p=0.02 (regression), fp8-dyn-v1 p=0.28 (not significant)
analysis: int8-asym-v1 represents a reasonable cost/quality tradeoff: small, non-significant quality drop with ~28% reduction in GPU memory bandwidth and ~18% lower token cost in inference benchmarks.
int8-asym-v2 overshot clipping aggressiveness leading to measurable degradation on long-tail queries (seen in adversarial_set).

fp8-dyn-v1 preserves quality almost identical to fp32 while giving modest latency improvements on A100 and H100 for our runtime; FP8 should be preferred for latency-critical short-sequence workloads where hardware support exists.

Per-layer analysis shows largest sensitivity in the final projection layers and attention output kernels; consider hybrid profiles that keep those layers at higher precision if more aggressive compression is required.
decisions: Adopt int8-asym-v1 as the default low-cost profile for batch-heavy, cost-sensitive reranker traffic with a staged canary rollout.
Adopt fp8-dyn-v1 for latency-sensitive routes and dedicated capacity tiers where hardware FP8 kernels are enabled.
Do not promote int8-asym-v2 due to regression risk on long-tail queries; keep it for internal experiments only.
Add per-route profile override in routing policy: route metadata key reranker.quant_profile with allowed values [fp32, fp8-dyn-v1, int8-asym-v1].
risks_mitigations: Risk: long-tail regressions not visible in small holdouts. Mitigation: 14-day canary with traffic-sampled telemetry and automated rollback if NDCG drop > 0.25 pp sustained for 3 hours.
Risk: hardware-specific FP8 numerical edge cases. Mitigation: run nightly multi-hardware cross-checks and keep per-hardware variant tags (fp8-h100, fp8-a100).
Risk: calibration drift as models update. Mitigation: include calibration as part of model release checklist; re-run calibration if model parameter delta > 0.5% L2 norm between checkpoints.
next_steps: 1) Publish int8-asym-v1 and fp8-dyn-v1 artifacts and update model-catalog entries with perf/cost tables (owner: Liam).
2) Wire QA harness into Console CI job to run nightly and create alert channels for metric breaches (owner: Suki).
3) Prepare canary runbook and automation for 14-day canary with automatic rollback thresholds (owner: Platform SRE).
4) Add hybrid profile experiment to keep final projection in FP16 and rest INT8 and run A/B against int8-asym-v1 (owner: Research).
